description: Well-appointed room in the heart of the vibrant Alberta Arts district. Enjoy a well-equipped, small kitchenette, and clear-covered, second story deck covered with grapevines in the rafters!
host_about:
I love living in Portland. I get to ride my bike around town most days or work on house or yard projects. I usually do a range of sports during the week depending on the time of year--including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, running and cycling. 
However, my biggest sports passions are kitesurfing, rock climbing, and slacklining. I've been climbing for over 20 years and have put up many new climbing routes around Portland over the years. Depending on the time of year, I will have a slackline set up in the backyard. If you've never tried it, it's unlike any other balance sport...basically a single line trampoline that feels impossible at first, but is actually quite manageable after a bit of practice.
I like gardening and have spent the last 10 years or so transplanting and cultivating trees, shrubs and sedums at the house. There are all sorts of perennial edibles here--cherry, plum, persimmon, fig, blueberry, huckleberry, strawberry, pear, grape, asparagus, kiwi and raspberry. Feel free to sample anything that's in season!
I lived in Bolivia for a couple of years while I was in the Peace Corps and have traveled to about 50 countries since then. I like being an adventure traveler and enjoy hosting other travelers and visitors as well. 
I bought this house back in 2006 and it was practically unlivable. Then once I decided to replace all the plumbing, it was unlivable for about 3 months. doh! But that was years ago. name: Cozy Alberta Arts Rm - hd TV, A/C, fast Wifi, Desk
description: A cozy bedroom with all the essentials and a bit of charm, located in the vibrant and eclectic Alberta Arts neighborhood.
host_about:
I love living in Portland. I get to ride my bike around town most days or work on house or yard projects. I usually do a range of sports during the week depending on the time of year--including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, running and cycling. 
However, my biggest sports passions are kitesurfing, rock climbing, and slacklining. I've been climbing for over 20 years and have put up many new climbing routes around Portland over the years. Depending on the time of year, I will have a slackline set up in the backyard. If you've never tried it, it's unlike any other balance sport...basically a single line trampoline that feels impossible at first, but is actually quite manageable after a bit of practice.
I like gardening and have spent the last 10 years or so transplanting and cultivating trees, shrubs and sedums at the house. There are all sorts of perennial edibles here--cherry, plum, persimmon, fig, blueberry, huckleberry, strawberry, pear, grape, asparagus, kiwi and raspberry. Feel free to sample anything that's in season!
I lived in Bolivia for a couple of years while I was in the Peace Corps and have traveled to about 50 countries since then. I like being an adventure traveler and enjoy hosting other travelers and visitors as well. 
I bought this house back in 2006 and it was practically unlivable. Then once I decided to replace all the plumbing, it was unlivable for about 3 months. doh! But that was years ago. These days, I continue to work on smallish projects around the house, whether it's transplanting my bamboo, adding a new gravel path, refinishing the 100yr old fir floors, planning a new garden bed, or building a covered bike storage area out of recycled materials.

name: Authentic Portland, Levity Lodge #3
description:
Bright, Private room with a King size lofted bed, lightly Shared bath, adjacent a flavorful, Peaceful feeling, owner-occupied central NE craftsman Home.
Welcome!
host_about:
Howdy Do! 
Big Fan of people here, glad to meet and have at least brief interactions and cerebral interludes with the whole sh'bang and gamut of characters this planet provides.  Travel feeds me well.  Another way to get that vitamin supplement from life in the times between travelings is to be part of another's adventure in some small way.  Hence, my own fondness for travel and the moments of feeling at home in the most remote stretches of the world is what brings me to AirBnB.  

I have warm, inviting space to spare, as well as energy and ideas about this pretty city that I dug so much I had to buy a little plot in it for myself and to SHARE with YOU!  Portland is beautiful.  I hope to make your travel far more enjoyable with a relaxing home base to replenish in between forays into the wild fray!
My darling, trusty, sweetheart William is my able co-host and a sweet addition to the casa's general goodness!
He is a fine horticulturalist and hobbyist filmmaker..
Also as of 2015 we have a son who is an awesome component of the tapestry around here. Our resting space is separate from the rest of the house for the most part, but we do share common space daily as well.
I do a little work from the home a couple days a week, but it ought never interfere with your autonomous fun having whilst here.  Let me know if I can help you with anything.

Personally~
 I'm an easy-moving, joyful, well-adjusted, silly critter, musician, painter, cook, writerly sort, interested in health and wholeness, Chinese herbal medicine (the eternal study continues!) and Acupuncture. I'm a traveler, an explorer, innate documentarian and story gatherer.  I'm handy, oft DIY-style, prefer  repurposing and re-using things and building materials in my projects.  
 I appreciate, to the point of deep reverence, the natural world's offerings and feel compelled to protect it with conscious consumption and recycling etc. I love clever design, architecture and texture in living/ working/ growing spaces as well.  Fond of dirt, making food and flora in it.  
Plenty to do in the loosely sketched canvas that a piece of land provides. If it suits your fancy, feel free to join me gardening during your stay. It's always fun to putter about in the yard with folks!

See you soon, with any luck!
-Leo

PS~ Incase you've wondered: I think I've got a good lead on what the meaning of life is. 
Wanna hear it?
To Give Exchange and Explore Loving Energy as Earnestly, Thoroughly and Frequently as Possible is Why We are Here.
Feels about right to me, so I figure we may as well move about the cabin in kindness, gathering recipes, hugs, soul food, stories and songs along the way!

host_about:
I love living in Portland. I get to ride my bike around town most days or work on house or yard projects. I usually do a range of sports during the week depending on the time of year--including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, running and cycling. 
However, my biggest sports passions are kitesurfing, rock climbing, and slacklining. I've been climbing for over 20 years and have put up many new climbing routes around Portland over the years. Depending on the time of year, I will have a slackline set up in the backyard. If you've never tried it, it's unlike any other balance sport...basically a single line trampoline that feels impossible at first, but is actually quite manageable after a bit of practice.
I like gardening and have spent the last 10 years or so transplanting and cultivating trees, shrubs and sedums at the house. There are all sorts of perennial edibles here--cherry, plum, persimmon, fig, blueberry, huckleberry, strawberry, pear, grape, asparagus, kiwi and raspberry. Feel free to sample anything that's in season!
I lived in Bolivia for a couple of years while I was in the Peace Corps and have traveled to about 50 countries since then. I like being an adventure traveler and enjoy hosting other travelers and visitors as well. 
I bought this house back in 2006 and it was practically unlivable. Then once I decided to replace all the plumbing, it was unlivable for about 3 months. doh! But that was years ago. These days, I continue to work on smallish projects around the house, whether it's transplanting my bamboo, adding a new gravel path, refinishing the 100yr old fir floors, planning a new garden bed, or building a covered bike storage area out of recycled materials.

name: Maple Cottage PDX/ Fun Historic Mississippi Ave.
description:
The Maple Cottage is located in the Historic Mississippi district of Portland. It offers a full kitchen, bedroom and generous dining room table that doubles as a work area. Just outside, is a small patio great for enjoying the garden. Restaurants and pubs are just a step away. Let's not forget Blue Star donuts!
Downtown Portland is just a short distance and our city is widely known for it's excellent transit system. Bikes are available for rent just a few blocks away.
Welcome to our home!
host_about:
We are a long term couple who have made Portland our home for over 20 years. The beauty of this place continues to knock our socks off! Getting out to hike, bike or kayak is a natural draw for us. Picnicking on the Wahclella Falls trail or kayaking on Lost Lake with Mt. Hood shining in the distance are favorite places.  When we get home we can walk to a nearby Thai bistro, Monsoon and pick up some Pumpkin Curry.  And there's also pizza and beer at the Kennedy School movie house. We love to walk out the door and wander down historic Mississippi Avenue for breakfast -- crepes at FlapJak or creme brulee oatmeal at Gravy.  Maybe we'll catch one of the seasonal events there like the Mardi Gras parade, Mississippi Street Fair or the Naked Bike Ride. 
But we also love hanging with friends or watching one of our favorite Netflix shows like 'Miss Fisher's Mystery Theatre'. I'm currently semi-retired and Marilyn is fully retired as of October 2016. We have plenty of time to welcome folks to our charming cottage and be available as needed. Chances are we can answer your questions or point you in the right direction.
Our motto is JAFA, Baby! (when you meet us, ask us what it means!)

name: Studio Apartment PandaCrystalCave
description:

host_about:
Ciao People!

I love traveling and I LOVE even more being a host of travelers - whatever brings you on your journey, work or love or experience!

I started traveling by myself when I was 18 in 1989. Long before there was email and all of the cool things to support backpackers today, I had traveled many places; I survived and thrived because people gave me food, took me around, gave me lodging, rides to the airport and took care of me when I got sick. So, I am always looking for the opportunity to help people out on their journeys!

My greatest travel passion is visiting national parks in eastern and southern Africa - so far I have been to 17 parks and I am in love with African wildlife and cultures.

But besides Africa, I love SE Asia culture - especially the food; I love Italian culture - especially the language; and, more than anything, I want to go to Mongolia, Bhutan, Khazakstan and Wales.

I am very much into the Slow philosophy as a lifestyle - I am an avid gardener and adventurously good cook.  

My biggest dream is to travel the world via dirigible.

As your host at PandaFaerie House here in Portland on Mt. Tabor, you will always find local roasted micro lot organic fair trade coffee or organic hand picked tea, a nearly complete Charles Bukowski collection for your reading voyeurism and a totally friendly greeting committee comprised of my dog, Bunny aka TACO.

name: St. Johns Farmhouse
description:
Our home is simple, cozy and welcoming and people generally feel immediately at ease. It is walking distance to historical St. Johns, and 1-3 blocks from bus lines. By TriMet it's 25 minutes to downtown and 50 minutes to the airport. This is a peaceful street with great neighbors who all know each other and look out for one another.
The bed is very comfortable, and most guests say they've gotten a great night's sleep!
The room is upstairs, and the bathroom is at the bottom of the stairs.
host_about:
I am someone who tries to live life full! I believe it is a gift that should be cherished through respect of others and myself. I would not want to live without great friends, great food, worthy projects that stimulate my creativity, my health and my home. 
I have traveled fairly extensively in Mexico and speak simple Spanish. I've also been to Europe, Canada, Hawaii and Alaska. 
I love to cook and most meals are made at home with fresh meat and vegetables (some from my garden).
I love meeting people from other countries and have been a "homestay" host to students from Japan and Saudi Arabia. I also had a lovely Persian woman renting my spare room for about a year. I have always done my best to make my guests feel a part of the family and give them the opportunity to experience the best of American life.
When I travel I usually go by public transit and would say I keep it on the cheap in general. I like to be close to the center of the action, but also enjoy going to the countryside.
My life motto is, "life is too short to be dull, so embrace it with excellence and make as many memories as possible!"

My partner Karen (who co-manages our listings) does community outreach, marketing, and large group mediation.  She is an amazing cook, a nascent wine expert, a hiker, movie buff, and part time caregiver for her mom.

I love dancing tango, painting, hunting for mushrooms, sipping tea and learning languages.

host_about:
Having lived in Portland since 1976, we think it's absolutely the BEST city around and we are always excited to share it with others! Don't just take our word for it: Portland was the ONLY U.S. City to be voted in 2015 as one of the top 25 most livable cities around the world and 2022 TOP Foodie City in U.S. 

We started hosting Airbnb in May, 2016 and are so deeply touched and humbled by the amazing guests we've met so far and look forward to those of you we've yet to meet.  We absolutely love entertaining and sharing the many treasures of Portland and the great Pacific NW with others.  

As fairly seasoned travelers ourselves, we also know what makes for a great stay and are invested in providing that for YOU as our guests.  

Now that we're retired from being public servants for years, we have lots more time for our hobbies and travels. You'll often find us being "groupies" for The RT’s; our son's band. The RT’s play energetic and thought-filled originals that blend New Orleans Jazz, Delta Blues and Rock and Roll.  Before the pandemic they played concerts and festivals all over the world and now, when covid permits, they may even be touring near your city.   Who knows?!  One day you might be able to say "I slept in the Portland Home of The R T's!" 

Portland's own musical treasures, The Norman Sylvester Band, keeps us dancing (we're teaching ourselves swing dance from youtube) to the blues around Portland.

Want to learn how to make wine?  Be a guest next Fall and go wine picking at a picture perfect u-pick farm; Z Farm-Hubbard. In September we picked over 1300 pounds of Pinot Noir grapes and always make it quite a party.  We've made wine for the last 11 years.  Bob also makes some of the best beer around from our homegrown hops.

Enough about our adventures; here's to YOUR NEW ADVENTURES!

name: Sunny  Mt Tabor 1 BR Suite. Walk to HIP Montavilla
description: This ENTIRE private street level apartment is steps from one of Portland's best parks.  And it's just a few blocks from public transportation, has easy freeway access, is pretty near the airport, and is close enough to downtown to make that an easy trip also.  It is walkable to Montavilla, one of the funnest pockets of local pub scene, boasting Breweries, Pubs, Restaurants, one of Portland's best Cocktail Bars, Dive Bars, and shopping, all condensed within a VERY strollable 3 or 4 block area.
host_about:
I'm a freelance video editor and home builder.   I'm friendly, but respectful of a person's private space.   I'm very into walking (I hike in Mt. Tabor park every morning), photography, racquetball, reading, movies, and craft breweries, of which there seem to be no end around here.  I like socializing, and getting out to see what this amazing city has to offer!

Meeting my guests is like having a little holiday without leaving Portland, as I get to hear what their home countries or regions are like.  This is the best part of Airbnb, and what keeps me excited to open my home to people from all different walks of life.  It's a pleasure and an honor to have people stay at my place, especially guests who are visiting this lovely country for the first time.   I also travel as much as I can, with an eye for what makes for a terrific stay, and incorporating the best of the great ideas I run across at other Airbnbs I see. 

My partner Karen (who co-manages our listings) does community outreach, marketing, and large group mediation.  She is an amazing cook, a nascent wine expert, a hiker, movie buff, and part time caregiver for her mom.

We can give you lots of ideas about pubs, restaurants, hikes, things to do while you are in Portland, but we am also fine leaving you alone to explore on your own, if you would prefer that.  There are a TON of different food types and styles within walking distance of here.

I believe the best of life really happens when you're outside.  But if the weather won't behave, this great house at least allows one to sit in front of a cozy fireplace and look out at the amazing view and watch the world go by.

Julie and Bob

host_about: I am a fun, easy-going guy who loves to travel to new places, spend time outdoors and stay physically and mentally healthy. I try to travel as much as possible and would really enjoy living seasonally at some point in my life. I am a field service engineer for a global manufacturer of photo-lithography systems for the semiconductor industry (if this leaves your head spinning don't feel bad, I hardly even know what that description entails!). My job allows me to travel frequently, both for work and pleasure, leading me to new experiences in places I never dreamed of visiting only a few years ago. I am an avid snowboarder and powder junkie during the winter months, while during the warmer seasons I mountain bike and cycle recreationaly. I typically travel light and prefer to explore any new environment either on foot or by bike with minimal planning. I enjoy visiting both cities as well as more remote destinations - and I truly believe the best way to experience any location is not necessarily to hit all the tourist spots, but rather take suggestions from area residents and do as they may on any normal day.

name: Alberta Arts - fast Wifi, hd TV, A/C - Great area!
description: Lovely room with a large south-facing window, comfortable bed, mini fridge and microwave. Located in the vibrant and eclectic Alberta Arts neighborhood.
host_about:
I love living in Portland. I get to ride my bike around town most days or work on house or yard projects. I usually do a range of sports during the week depending on the time of year--including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, running and cycling. 
However, my biggest sports passions are kitesurfing, rock climbing, and slacklining. I've been climbing for over 20 years and have put up many new climbing routes around Portland over the years. Depending on the time of year, I will have a slackline set up in the backyard. If you've never tried it, it's unlike any other balance sport...basically a single line trampoline that feels impossible at first, but is actually quite manageable after a bit of practice.
I like gardening and have spent the last 10 years or so transplanting and cultivating trees, shrubs and sedums at the house. There are all sorts of perennial edibles here--cherry, plum, persimmon, fig, blueberry, huckleberry, strawberry, pear, grape, asparagus, kiwi and raspberry. Feel free to sample anything that's in season!
I lived in Bolivia for a couple of years while I was in the Peace Corps and have traveled to about 50 countries since then. I like being an adventure traveler and enjoy hosting other travelers and visitors as well.

description: Stylish little house with lots of light and lots of garden! Clean, comfortable space where anyone could enjoy a relaxing vacation. A short walk to some of Portland’s favorite restaurants and bars! Littlebluepdx does not disappoint!
host_about:
A little bit about little blue.
Adam, my husband and I bought a house  6 years ago -a couple of weeks before I gave birth to our little firecracker of a daughter Mabel 
We took a 1907 weathered house + tiny garage, ripped it to the studs and built them back up again. Adam wanted to do the work himself but also wanted to start a design agency. I'll spare you guys the drama in between- but as you can imagine: new baby, new business, renovation and no family close by took its toll.
But......


Adam, a thru-hiker has collected some of the most amazing friends. We wanted clean sheets + a cozy bed for them. Me, a family girl from the south wanted space for her parents + siblings.
And while our original intent was to take care of the people we know- it’s actually turned into this lovely space for new friends. And we couldn’t be happier!

We love the space because it represents the end of a very  long journey. And while the story brought out the best and the worst in us- it's all the good stuff that makes us want to be a community for travelers. It's the late night porch chats over oregon pinot and saying hello to perfect strangers that made us keep going.

We want you all to enjoy our space and make it your own. We want to hear your stories- whether face to face or written in our tiny journal.

Please, make yourselves at home.

Libby, Adam & Mabel

Selena :)

name: Grant Park Haven in NE Portland
description: Welcome to Grant Park Haven, your home away from home.  Located in the beautiful Grant Park/Hollywood neighborhood of NE Portland, it offers easy access to downtown, public transportation, restaurants, pubs, shopping, entertainment, parks, a swimming pool, grocery stores, and the freeways. The one bedroom Airbnb is the day-lit, lower unit of a new Craftsman style house built in 2018. With a queen bed and a queen sofabed in the living area, there is space for 4 people total.  Everyone is welcome!
host_about:
Hello!  I am an active, involved, long-time Portland resident who loves the easy access to nature that our city offers. Our beautiful parks, strong neighborhood communities, many cultural events and organizations, our commitment to recycling and sustainability, the Multnomah County Library and Powell's Bookstore, and the river that runs through downtown are also wonderful assets that I love.

One of the many reasons I am looking forward to being an Airbnb host is being able to offer the same opportunities I have enjoyed as a guest staying in others' Airbnbs, Bed and Breakfasts, hostels, and hotels all over the world. I've lived in France (Paris one spring and in Bordeaux for my junior year of university) and have traveled extensively throughout Europe and Asia. I have also traveled in Canada, Mexico, Central America, Morocco, Kenya, and Ecuador as well as almost every state in the US.   In opening up Grant Park Haven, I look forward to offering you the same opportunity to connect across cultures, and will do my very best to make sure you are very comfortable!

Singing and music bring great joy to my life.  Currently I sing with the Portland Threshold Singers, a group that offers comfort and support to people at bedside, most often at the end of life. In the past, I've sung with choirs of all kinds, as well as with friends and the folk music community.  Gardening, contradancing, camping, hiking, backpacking, and swimming are also some of the things that I greatly enjoy.  I volunteer at the library, and with other community organizations. I also take pleasure in and appreciate connecting with people from all walks of life through good conversations over a cup of tea or coffee, or a glass of wine.

I have been a Licensed Massage Therapist for 43 years.

My aspiration is to live this amazing life I've been given with kindness, empathy, deep listening, and joy.  I look forward to meeting you, and to sharing Portland with you.

Kate

Liz & Grant

host_about:
I moved to Oregon from Michigan. I have found home here with the ocean, the mountains and the city...a perfect trio! I live with my fun-loving, adventurous husband who also moved here from the midwest. name: 2BR Suite on Alberta St in hip art district
description:
The Alberta Petite Hotel is a very nice relaxing house in a perfect walkable location on Alberta St and 24th with galleries, local shops, restaurants and entertainment.
This quaint space is a private daylight basement with its own external entrance, living area with TV, bathroom, dining area and kitchenette. Enjoy the outdoor sitting spaces for relaxing and people watching. One parking space.
host_about:
Robin and Brian love to stay in unique, small and interesting lodging facilities where they meet people from all over the world and learn about local cultures. And frankly, they would travel a lot more given the opportunity. So they decided..."why not bring the 'travel' to us?" 

They wanted to create a cool space where people experience that same 'travel adventure' feeling  right here in Portland. So they took the plunge and found a house they could convert, in one of the hippest neighborhoods in Portland - The Alberta Arts District, where there is an abundance of amazing restaurants, cool shops, food carts, a theater, bike shops, coffee houses and so much to offer tourists.

An important part of their vision was to create a fun, warm, comfortable, safe and open space for people from all walks of life - for women, people of color, the LGBTQ+ community, immigrant populations, international travelers, etc. Additionally, the well-being of the planet was extremely important to them when creating the space. Therefore, a lot of time, effort and resources went into making this business as sustainable and environmentally-responsible as possible. That means they worked very hard to make sure the materials, furnishings and products that were purchased were top-quality, reused or salvaged when possible, organically grown, sustainably-sourced, made by local people, etc. Another aspect they are focusing on is to showcase Portland by utilizing Portland artisans and sustainable Portland-created products.

They hope you'll consider staying in their little hotel and experience the awesome neighborhood it's located in.

host_about:
Hello! I'm Jodi (pronouns: she/her)

As host, I'm keen to help make your experience in Portland as comfortable and homey as possible. I enjoy sharing my tranquil backyard setting with guests and have a healthy appreciation for a balance of both adventure and quiet solitude.

And I'm always open to answer more questions should you have them! : )

name: Alberta Arts Renov. 110-yr old  Apt - fast Wifi!
description: Lovely, craftsman, renovated 1907 Portland home. The main floor of a 3-level house is all yours to enjoy. An earthy, rough-tiled, slate floor, leads past an up-cycled timber roof truss, into the living room, with refurbished old-growth, fir floors and authentic ax mark blemishes. Once, a nearly abandoned old house, in a tough neighborhood, it now glows with rejuvenation inside and the vibrant, eccentric, internationally-recognized , Alberta Arts neighborhood a few blocks away.
host_about:
I love living in Portland. I get to ride my bike around town most days or work on house or yard projects. I usually do a range of sports during the week depending on the time of year--including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, running and cycling. 
However, my biggest sports passions are kitesurfing, rock climbing, and slacklining. I've been climbing for over 20 years and have put up many new climbing routes around Portland over the years. Depending on the time of year, I will have a slackline set up in the backyard. If you've never tried it, it's unlike any other balance sport...basically a single line trampoline that feels impossible at first, but is actually quite manageable after a bit of practice.
I like gardening and have spent the last 10 years or so transplanting and cultivating trees, shrubs and sedums at the house. There are all sorts of perennial edibles here--cherry, plum, persimmon, fig, blueberry, huckleberry, strawberry, pear, grape, asparagus, kiwi and raspberry. Feel free to sample anything that's in season!
I lived in Bolivia for a couple of years while I was in the Peace Corps and have traveled to about 50 countries since then. I like being an adventure traveler and enjoy hosting other travelers and visitors as well. 
I bought this house back in 2006 and it was practically unlivable. Then once I decided to replace all the plumbing, it was unlivable for about 3 months. doh! But that was years ago. These days, I continue to work on smallish projects around the house, whether it's transplanting my bamboo, adding a new gravel path, refinishing the 100yr old fir floors, planning a new garden bed, or building a covered bike storage area out of recycled materials.

name: 📚🗺🐈‍⬛ Local History Museum in Historic Albina
description:
Built in 1895 in the Historic Albina neighborhood, our home has oft been described as a local history library full of maps and books to help you get the most local flavor possible during your stay in Portland.

As a seventh-generation Oregonian, I’ve hosted travelers from all seven continents, and am excited to share this local knowledge with everyone who comes into our home.
host_about:
I'm a Traffic Engineer with years of experience bicycle touring, and as a result CouchSurfing and now Airbnb.

I’ve hosted guests in my home from six continents, with travels spanning six continents over more than a decade.

If you're planning a bike tour anywhere in and around the Portland metro area, or anywhere in Oregon and Washington, I'd be more than happy to give you plenty of tips.



In the summer of 2009, I cycled over 1,000 miles around Washington state and 1,500 miles down the Pacific Coast to Mexico, including my first time CouchSurfing. In the summer of 2010, I cycled over 4,000 miles from Portland, Oregon to New York City. Since then, I've done smaller tours all over Oregon and Washington, including a week around Central Oregon, a three-day marathon of 400 miles up I-5 to Canada, and a few days on the northern Oregon coast, to name a few. In 2013, I cycled for two months through a dozen countries in Western Europe. More recent excursions include many trips through the islands of Puget Sound, including multiple rides between Seattle and Bellingham, all over the San Juans, as well as the Gulf Islands and Vancouver Island. In 2018, I cycled across England en route from Amsterdam to Dublin via Dover and the Isle of Man.

name: The Woodstock Guest House
description: Perfect for families and professionals, our newly renovated guest house is a great place to relax after a hard day of work or play. Get an excellent night’s sleep on the memory foam mattresses. Enjoy the steam in the enormous walk-in shower. Kick back on the patio with a brew from Double Mountain Taproom. Create a gourmet meal with produce from the Portland Farmer’s Market. Snuggle up by the fire with a good book from Powell’s. Unwind at the Woodstock Guest House by booking today!
host_about:
My hobbies vary greatly, but include hiking, camping, juggling, watching both art-house films and really bad action/adventure flicks, eating ice cream, bicycling, singing, dancing, playing with kids, roughhousing with the dogs, BBQs, reading, eating yummy things, traveling, writing, and going on adventures. I am at peace when surrounded by trees, mountains, and water. 

Below is an excerpt from my travel journal. To read more of my adventures, visit www.oddkazoo.com. 

We are Indiana Jones! We are National Geographic! We are fearless explorers! A hike through the jungle and then we are swimming (swimming!) into the vast maw of a cave, helmets and headlamps, absolute darkness with the lights off. No difference between eyes open and eyes closed. We splash along an underground river, sometimes knee deep, sometimes treading across deep pools, squeezing under boulders, into fissures, over rockslides, the stalactites sometimes brushing the tops of our heads, sometimes towering ninety feet above. Crystaline rock flows, sparkling in the glow of our tiny lights, shadows and browns and greys and greens. 

We are travelers in Xibalba, the ancient Mayan underworld. 

After an hour we climb a rock face, steeper steeper higher higher onto a plateau, cavernous, winding, bats, space, darkness, the headlamps barely piercing the depth of the darkness. And then, and then! There is a jug, half buried in the calcite. And there is a metate, and a plate and a bowl and they are impeccable and painted and carved and 1200 YEARS OLD, all just resting on the ground, not behind glass, no railings, no ropes, no signs. The archeologists left everything just as they found it, untouched, a living breathing museum, and I am imagining the elite Mayans with their bloodletting and sacrifices and ceremonies and everyone is whispering because this is a sacred place, a place of desperation for a failing civilization, a place of last hope for rain, please Chuc, rain. 

We traverse the flats amongst a hundred hundred artifacts, and then there is a ladder, which brings us to a deep alcove, high within the cave. Ten steps and there she is, the Crystal Maiden, a young woman, sacrficied to the gods, her bones crystalized and perfect. She lies with her legs straight but her arms splayed. Her mouth is wide open. She was strangled to death. And she is still there in her dark and cool and cavernous tomb, and we are there, breathing softly, averting our eyes out of respect for the dead, but also longing to watch the bones, watch their stillness. We turn back and she is once more plunged into darkness and I tremble as I descend the ladder.

description:

host_about:
Gary here... a very friendly, easy going, and welcoming fellow who truly loves the Airbnb experience both as a traveler and especially as a host to guests from around the world.  My first guests arrived in November of 2013 and I've since opened my front door to over 1400 others from 25 countries.  Each of my guest rooms are cozy, welcoming, and unique.  I have a simple goal to provide a comfortable, special, and inviting place to call "home" when visiting our beautiful and vibrant city.  My guests are welcome to enjoy a movie in front of the fire in the living room, have a candlelit dinner in the dining room, cook up a tasty meal in the kitchen, and enjoy relaxing in the hot tub & yard surrounded by fountains, flowers, greenery, and serenity.
I'm really just a renaissance man. I've worked as a high school teacher, a behavioral health therapist, small business owner, gardener, builder/thinker/crafter, and most passionately as a professional actor for 40 years, mostly in musical theatre but also on camera.  ** I'm also a grateful "friend of Bill W."
I've always enjoyed meeting new people.  Local theatre, music, books, restaurants, being outdoors, gardening, movies, are just a few pieces of my life (not forgetting karaoke).  I also love a road trip, traveling, any "water destination" (ocean, river, lake, stream, or pool!), and enjoying the sunshine whether it's in my convertible, on a hike, diggin' in the garden, or just a walk.  I do clean up quite well and can be found in a suit & tie, or even a tuxedo. 
My home, URBAN HAVEN as I call it, is my castle!  I share it with my two adorable pups, SeeBee & Mannie; they're really my kids.  I'm also caregiver for my dad, Gary Sr., who spent a decade on the streets of Santa Cruz County until 7 years of searching led me to him.  Dad is a quiet and extremely kind man enjoying our being together and grateful for his 2nd chance at life.  
I take extreme pride in my simple home of 22 years. I welcome every guest with a smile and a "make yourself at home, relax & enjoy,"  invitation.  I'm happy to give suggestions of things to do and see, let guests explore on their own, and even get suggestions from my guests about "what's new" that I haven't even seen yet myself.
I consider myself a very genuine and authentic gentleman with healthy sense of humor,  with a goofy and even mildly devilish side.

name: 3BR Spacious hm on Alberta St in cool art district
description: The Alberta Petite Hotel is a very nice relaxing house in a perfect walkable location on Alberta St and 24th with galleries, local shops, restaurants and entertainment. The house is craftsman-style with modern and contemporary touches. host_about:
Robin and Brian love to stay in unique, small and interesting lodging facilities where they meet people from all over the world and learn about local cultures. And frankly, they would travel a lot more given the opportunity. So they decided..."why not bring the 'travel' to us?" 

They wanted to create a cool space where people experience that same 'travel adventure' feeling  right here in Portland. So they took the plunge and found a house they could convert, in one of the hippest neighborhoods in Portland - The Alberta Arts District, where there is an abundance of amazing restaurants, cool shops, food carts, a theater, bike shops, coffee houses and so much to offer tourists.

An important part of their vision was to create a fun, warm, comfortable, safe and open space for people from all walks of life - for women, people of color, the LGBTQ+ community, immigrant populations, international travelers, etc. Additionally, the well-being of the planet was extremely important to them when creating the space. Therefore, a lot of time, effort and resources went into making this business as sustainable and environmentally-responsible as possible. That means they worked very hard to make sure the materials, furnishings and products that were purchased were top-quality, reused or salvaged when possible, organically grown, sustainably-sourced, made by local people, etc. Another aspect they are focusing on is to showcase Portland by utilizing Portland artisans and sustainable Portland-created products.

They hope you'll consider staying in their little hotel and experience the awesome neighborhood it's located in.

name: 5BR Modern Craftsman on artsy Alberta St
description: The Alberta Petite Hotel is a very nice relaxing house in a perfect walkable location on Alberta St and 24th with galleries, local shops, restaurants and entertainment. The house is craftsman-style with modern and contemporary touches. Rent the whole house which includes 5 bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms, a spacious and well-stocked kitchen, kitchenette in lower unit, large dining room, living room, laundry room and office. Enjoy the expansive porch and the many outdoor spaces. Plus two parking spaces.
host_about:
Robin and Brian love to stay in unique, small and interesting lodging facilities where they meet people from all over the world and learn about local cultures. And frankly, they would travel a lot more given the opportunity. So they decided..."why not bring the 'travel' to us?" 

They wanted to create a cool space where people experience that same 'travel adventure' feeling  right here in Portland. So they took the plunge and found a house they could convert, in one of the hippest neighborhoods in Portland - The Alberta Arts District, where there is an abundance of amazing restaurants, cool shops, food carts, a theater, bike shops, coffee houses and so much to offer tourists.

An important part of their vision was to create a fun, warm, comfortable, safe and open space for people from all walks of life - for women, people of color, the LGBTQ+ community, immigrant populations, international travelers, etc. Additionally, the well-being of the planet was extremely important to them when creating the space. Therefore, a lot of time, effort and resources went into making this business as sustainable and environmentally-responsible as possible. That means they worked very hard to make sure the materials, furnishings and products that were purchased were top-quality, reused or salvaged when possible, organically grown, sustainably-sourced, made by local people, etc. Another aspect they are focusing on is to showcase Portland by utilizing Portland artisans and sustainable Portland-created products.

They hope you'll consider staying in their little hotel and experience the awesome neighborhood it's located in.

name: Treetop Craftsman Over Garden
description:
Keep it simple at this peaceful and centrally-located place.
Step into a serene, top-floor apartment, set in a renovated craftsman house right in the heart of the bustling Alberta Arts district. The vine-draped, second-story porch, offers tranquil treetop views. It's an inviting escape, with the vibrant energy of the nearby, trendy Alberta Arts neighborhood.
host_about:
I love living in Portland. I get to ride my bike around town most days or work on house or yard projects. I usually do a range of sports during the week depending on the time of year--including basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee, running and cycling. 
However, my biggest sports passions are kitesurfing, rock climbing, and slacklining. I've been climbing for over 20 years and have put up many new climbing routes around Portland over the years. Depending on the time of year, I will have a slackline set up in the backyard. If you've never tried it, it's unlike any other balance sport...basically a single line trampoline that feels impossible at first, but is actually quite manageable after a bit of practice.
I like gardening and have spent the last 10 years or so transplanting and cultivating trees, shrubs and sedums at the house. There are all sorts of perennial edibles here--cherry, plum, persimmon, fig, blueberry, huckleberry, strawberry, pear, grape, asparagus, kiwi and raspberry. Feel free to sample anything that's in season!
I lived in Bolivia for a couple of years while I was in the Peace Corps and have traveled to about 50 countries since then. I like being an adventure traveler and enjoy hosting other travelers and visitors as well. 
I bought this house back in 2006 and it was practically unlivable. Then once I decided to replace all the plumbing, it was unlivable for about 3 months. doh! But that was years ago. These days, I continue to work on smallish projects around the house, whether it's transplanting my bamboo, adding a new gravel path, refinishing the 100yr old fir floors, planning a new garden bed, or building a covered bike storage area out of recycled materials.

description: This ENTIRE private street level 1BR home is steps from one of Portland's best parks. host_about:

Tabor park every morning), photography, racquetball, reading, movies, and craft breweries, of which there seem to be no end around here. Meeting my guests is like having a little holiday without leaving Portland, as I get to hear what their home countries or regions are like.  This is the best part of Airbnb, and what keeps me excited to open my home to people from all different walks of life.  It's a pleasure and an honor to have people stay at my place, especially guests who are visiting this lovely country for the first time.   I also travel as much as I can, with an eye for what makes for a terrific stay, and incorporating the best of the great ideas I run across at other Airbnbs I see. 

My partner Karen (who co-manages our listings) does community outreach, marketing, and large group mediation.  She is an amazing cook, a nascent wine expert, a hiker, movie buff, and part time caregiver for her mom.

We can give you lots of ideas about pubs, restaurants, hikes, things to do while you are in Portland, but we am also fine leaving you alone to explore on your own, if you would prefer that.  There are a TON of different food types and styles within walking distance of here.

I believe the best of life really happens when you're outside.  But if the weather won't behave, this great house at least allows one to sit in front of a cozy fireplace and look out at the amazing view and watch the world go by.
